image_description: A side-profile view of an adult American bison standing on a gravel path next to a grassy field. The background features rolling hills and sparse trees under a blue sky. A second, smaller bison is visible in the distant background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large broad head with short curved horns.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible in profile; it is large and broad relative to the body, and short, dark, curved horns are distinct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beard of long hair on chin and throat.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A prominent, shaggy beard hangs from the chin and throat area, consistent with bison anatomy.
The eye is visible as a dark spot within the heavy facial fur.
Ears are not prominently sticking out; they appear small and blend into the thick mane/fur around the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Massive body with exceptionally tall, heavily built proportions at the withers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The animal exhibits the characteristic massive build, appearing heavy and robust.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Shaggy dark brown fur covering forequarters forming prominent shoulder hump.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is a very distinct, high shoulder hump covered in thick, shaggy dark brown fur, which is the defining feature of the species.
The fur on the rear half of the body is visibly shorter and smoother compared to the dense mane on the front.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Short horns compared to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The horns are relatively small and short in proportion to the massive head and body.
All four legs are visible, appearing sturdy and black/dark. While individual hoof splits are hard to resolve at this resolution, the general shape and stance are correct for a bovid.
The tail is visible hanging down, ending in a distinct dark, bushy switch/tuft.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species classification (American Bison vs. European Bison or other bovids) and rule out misclassification artifacts.
To verify the structural integrity of the four legs and ensure no fusion or extra limbs exist, despite the heavy fur obscuring joints.
To check for subtle texture inconsistencies in the fur transition zones and background blending.
To ensure the background mountains have consistent geometry and do not show warping or melting typical of AI generation.

focus_areas: Shoulder hump morphology and fur density transition
Leg structure and hoof grounding on gravel
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the transition between the shaggy forequarter fur and the smoother hindquarter fur; AI often blurs this boundary unnaturally. Verify that the legs do not 'melt' into the gravel or each other. Check if the distant bison has coherent anatomy or appears as a blob.
